subject: Calibra latency spike: fallback playbook, product tradeoffs & customer note
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam@calibra.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@calibra.com
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High p95 latency starting 08:45 PST — immediate help needed

Olga / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase on our gen-text endpoint at ~08:45 PST. Error rate is low but median is fine; the user-facing complaints are about slow responses (>3s p95) and a few timeouts. This is impacting a small percentage of checkout flows.

Quick facts:
- Region: us-west-2
- Model: stable-2027-large (pinned)
- Traffic: 120% of baseline for the hour
- First noticed in production: 08:45 PST

Can you confirm if this is a known degradation or if we should expect a fallback? We need an ETA for mitigation and a short customer-facing note to share with our support team.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Carter
Sr. Platform Engineer, Calibra
[Attachment: calibra_kpi_logs.csv]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: RE: High p95 latency starting 08:45 PST — immediate help needed

Team — looping you in. Calibra (external) reported rising p95 at ~08:45 PST. Key asks: immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact + a concise customer note.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we can do 1+ in parallel):
- Short term routing: direct Calibra traffic to quantized-stable-2027 (lower-cost variant) for 30m — minimal quality regression but much lower latency.
- Prefix/KV cache: enable sticky prefix cache for known conversational flows (if safe) — will reduce repeated tokens.
- Rate-smoothing by key: apply a short token-rate cap for heavy clients to keep p95 stable.
- Fallback page: return lightweight apology + retry-with-backoff for requests exceeding 4s.

Product tradeoffs we need to surface to customer: quality delta (quantized variant), potential for transient cache warmup causing a brief spike, and any billing implications for request rerouting. I attached a draft fallback playbook — please review technical feasibility and risks.

Can Ben/Jonas give runbook ETA for each mitigation (mins), and Marissa can you approve a quick customer note draft if we can buy 20–30 minutes to implement?

Thanks — Ol
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fallback_playbook_v1.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Calibra latency spike: fallback playbook, product tradeoffs & customer note

Olga — quick summary from SRE perspective after 10m triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: scheduler contention on our multi-tenant pool in us-west-2 combined with a transient KV cache eviction. We see increased tail due to retries and queuing behind large-batched requests.

Feasible immediate actions + estimated time to safe rollout:
1) Route Calibra to quantized-stable-2027 (can flip traffic at the routing layer): ~15 minutes to test + 10 min monitoring window. Risk: small generation quality delta for long-context prompts.
2) Toggle prefix cache sticky mode (if caller patterns allow): ~8 minutes. Risk: if we mis-detect prefix shapes, cache misses may persist for a few minutes while warming.
3) Apply soft rate-smoothing (throttling burst windows) per API key via gateway: ~5 minutes to enable, but customer-visible error patterns if strict. Recommend soft quota enforcement with Retry-After header.
4) Fallback page / 4s timeout enforcement on edge: ~12 minutes to deploy rule, minimal model change risk but visible to end users.

Priority: 3 (rate-smoothing) + 1 (routing to quantized) => combined should reduce p95 within ~20–30 minutes. We'll push config changes carefully, monitor p95/median, and rollback if error rate increases.

I'll prepare the exact CLI commands and a guarded roll (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%). Jonas to help validate kernel selection/throughput impact for quantized variant.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam@calibra.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Feb 2028 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Customer note + ask: approve simple messaging for Calibra support

Liam — thanks for the heads up and patience while we worked through mitigation. Ben and team executed a guarded routing change to quantized-stable-2027 and enabled soft rate-smoothing; we observed p95 drop below 900ms after the canary.

Proposed customer-facing note (short) — pls review and tell me if you want this to go to your support portal now: 

---
Hi Calibra Support team,

We routed a portion of your traffic to a low-latency model variant and applied temporary rate-smoothing to reduce user-facing delays. You should see p95 latency return to expected levels. There is a small chance of quality difference on very long prompts while the routing change is in effect; we are monitoring and will revert when stable.

If you continue to see issues, please reply to this thread with sample request IDs and we’ll escalate immediately.

Best,
Olga (Redwood Inference)
---

Marissa/Ben/Jonas — approve copy? Also confirm: any billing impact we should flag (Marissa) and Ben, please paste the canary toggle commands & monitoring dashboard links in reply so I can include them in a short post-mortem.

Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: customer_note_draft.md]
